title_en: Li Linzhen v. Bank of China, Tonglu Branch — dispute over termination of labor contract

full_text_en:
Li Linzhen v. Tonglu Sub-branch of Bank of China — dispute over rescission of labor contract

Plaintiff: Li Linzhen, female, 28 years old, contract worker at Tonglu Sub-branch of Zhejiang Branch of Bank of China.

Agent ad litem: Wang Hansheng and Xu Jianyu, lawyers of Zhejiang Huaxia Law Firm.

Defendant: Tonglu Sub-branch of Zhejiang Branch of Bank of China.

Legal representative: Luo Bingfa, sub-branch manager.

Agent ad litem: Pu Fan, deputy sub-branch manager of Tonglu Sub-branch of Bank of China.

The plaintiff Li Linzhen brought an action before the Tonglu County People's Court of Zhejiang Province regarding a labor contract dispute with the defendant, Tonglu Sub-branch of Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Tonglu Sub-branch).

The plaintiff Li Linzhen alleged: On February 24, 1994, the defendant Tonglu Sub-branch unilaterally decided to rescind the labor contract on the grounds that the plaintiff lacked a right kidney, which was a serious physical defect. From the perspective of clinical medical practice, the lack of one kidney does not pose a serious threat to health as long as renal function is normal. The diagnosis from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang Medical University confirmed that the plaintiff's renal function was normal and she could work normally. In terms of the nature of banking work, the plaintiff was engaged in accounting work; the lack of one kidney would not pose any threat to her work, nor would it affect the external image required of a bank employee. Moreover, from the perspective of national physical examination policies, the "Physical Examination Standards for Enrollment in General Institutions of Higher Education" allow persons lacking one kidney to apply for any major except those in geology. In light of the above reasons, the plaintiff requested the court to revoke the defendant's decision to rescind the labor contract with the plaintiff and order the defendant to continue performing the labor contract.

The defendant Tonglu Sub-branch argued: The plaintiff Li Linzhen had undergone right kidney removal. She did not disclose this to the physician during the physical examination. After she joined our sub-branch, it was reported by others and confirmed by hospital reexamination. The plaintiff did not meet the recruitment conditions of "good health, free from serious diseases and defects" required for new employees under the "Provisional Provisions on Recruitment, Hiring, Transfer of Personnel and Probation of New Employees of Zhejiang Branch of Bank of China" (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisional Provisions"). According to relevant documents of the Ministry of Labor and Personnel, during the probation period, if a contract system worker is found not to meet the recruitment conditions, the employing unit has the right to unilaterally rescind the labor contract. The defendant believed that the plaintiff's removal of the right kidney constituted a serious defect, on the grounds that Bank of China has relatively high requirements for its employees, and it does not exclude the possibility that other industries might consider such a defect as a general defect and still hire the person. Accordingly, the defendant requested the court to uphold the defendant's decision to rescind Li Linzhen's labor contract, as set forth in Document Tongzhongyin (1994) No. 8.

The Tonglu County People's Court found through trial: The plaintiff Li Linzhen accidentally fell down stairs in 1987 and was injured, and underwent surgery to remove her right kidney at the hospital. After the surgery, she recovered her health. In early August 1993, Li Linzhen learned that the defendant Tonglu Sub-branch was recruiting workers. Believing she met the conditions, she registered for the recruitment. On August 16, after interviewing the applicants, Tonglu Sub-branch preliminarily decided that Li Linzhen could participate in the physical examination. On August 20, the defendant organized the preliminarily selected persons to undergo routine physical examinations at Tonglu County Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital. Li Linzhen's physical examination form recorded: "Past medical history" column: "no disability"; "Abdominal organs" column: "normal"; "Review opinion" column: "healthy." On August 23, Tonglu Sub-branch organized training for the preliminarily selected persons including Li Linzhen. On August 28, Tonglu Sub-branch assigned Li Linzhen to report to its Hengcun Office. On September 1, Tonglu Sub-branch and Li Linzhen signed a labor contract. The contract stipulated: The term of the labor contract was five years (from September 1, 1993 to August 31, 1998); job type: business; a six-month probation period; during the contract period, if the recruited contract system worker fell under the provisions of Article 12 of the "Provisional Regulations on the Implementation of the Labor Contract System in State-Owned Enterprises" (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract System Regulations") concerning "the enterprise may rescind the labor contract," the enterprise could propose to rescind the labor contract. The contract was signed by both Li Linzhen and Tonglu Sub-branch, and was notarized and became effective by the Labor Dispute Arbitration Section of Tonglu County Labor Bureau. In mid-December, the Hangzhou City Branch of Bank of China notified Tonglu Sub-branch by telephone that "someone reported that Li Linzhen had her right kidney removed, which does not meet the recruitment conditions," and required Tonglu Sub-branch to rescind the labor contract with Li Linzhen before the end of 1993. On December 26, Tonglu Sub-branch sent personnel to take Li Linzhen to Tonglu County Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital for a B-ultrasound examination. The result confirmed that Li Linzhen had "right kidney removed, left kidney normal." On February 24, 1994, Tonglu Sub-branch made a decision to rescind Li Linzhen's labor contract, Document Tongzhongyin (1994) No. 8, on the ground that Li Linzhen "had her right kidney removed, which is a serious physical defect, and did not meet the relevant requirements of the Provincial Branch's 'Provisional Provisions'." On August 11 of the same year, Li Linzhen applied for arbitration to the Tonglu County Labor Dispute Arbitration Commission. After hearing the case, the Tonglu County Labor Dispute Arbitration Commission issued an arbitration award, Document Tonglaozhongcaizi (1994) No. 1, on December 6, upholding Tonglu Sub-branch's decision to rescind Li Linzhen's labor contract. The plaintiff, dissatisfied, filed a lawsuit with the court on December 21. During the trial of this case, the court commissioned the Forensic Medical Technology Department of the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court to conduct an appraisal on whether Li Linzhen's body had serious defects. The forensic appraisal concluded: The appraised person Li Linzhen has a physiological defect of lacking a right kidney, but she has normal living ability, work ability, and social activity ability; her physical condition does not reach the level of serious defects.

The Tonglu County People's Court held: The plaintiff Li Linzhen had her right kidney removed due to injury, and indeed has a physiological defect of lacking a right kidney. The defendant Tonglu Sub-branch signed the labor contract with Li Linzhen without knowing that she lacked a right kidney, and now made a decision to rescind the labor contract on this ground. Article 12(1) of the "Contract System Regulations" provides that an enterprise may rescind the labor contract only if "during the probation period, a contract system worker is found not to meet the recruitment conditions." According to the forensic appraisal, Li Linzhen's physical condition did not reach the level of serious defects, and during the probation period, Li Linzhen was healthy and capable of performing the business tasks assigned by Tonglu Sub-branch. The above facts prove that Li Linzhen's physical condition met the recruitment condition of "no serious diseases and defects." The reason given by Tonglu Sub-branch that Li Linzhen had serious physical defects could not be established. Article 14(1) provides that "if the term of the labor contract has not expired and the conditions under Article 12 are not met," the enterprise shall not rescind the labor contract. Li Linzhen's claim to revoke the defendant's decision to rescind her labor contract and to continue performing the labor contract should be supported. Accordingly, the Tonglu County People's Court on December 1, 1995, rendered the following judgment:

1. Revoke the decision of the defendant Tonglu Sub-branch, Document Tongzhongyin (1994) No. 8, to rescind the labor contract of the plaintiff Li Linzhen.

2. The defendant Tonglu Sub-branch and the plaintiff Li Linzhen shall continue to perform the labor contract, Document Tonglaojianzi (1993) No. 1050.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the defendant Tonglu Sub-branch appealed to the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court on the same grounds as its defense.

The Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court held upon trial: The labor contract signed between the appellant Tonglu Sub-branch and the appellee Li Linzhen complied with relevant provisions and should be recognized as lawful and valid. It was a fact that Li Linzhen had her right kidney removed due to injury, but her physical condition did not reach the level of serious defects, and she could adapt to the work assigned to her. Her right to labor should be protected according to law. The appellant Tonglu Sub-branch's grounds for appeal could not be established. The first-instance judgment was correct and should be affirmed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court on January 30, 1996, rendered the following judgment: Dismiss the appeal of the appellant Tonglu Sub-branch and affirm the first-instance judgment.
